title: It's Not Easy Being Me (Chas McIvor)
style: country blues acoustic guitar warm baritone male vocal storytelling 104bpm walking bass brushed drums honest character portrait true story Australian resilience unhurried
lyrics:
[Intro - acoustic guitar, dry and honest, unhurried]
It's not easy being me.
Joel said that.
At eight in the morning.
Going to bed.
That's the whole song right there.

[Verse 1]
First grade rugby.
Neck surgery.
Sucker punch November twenty-one.
Broken leg at Christmas — Jack in the golf buggy.
That was not on the calendar.
Tricep muscle on the left arm
Still working itself out.
And he went to bed saying
It's not easy being me.

[Verse 2]
He texts his brother at midnight
From the other side of the country
Just calling to wish you the best in the new year
Gives the kids a kiss on their forehead in absentia
Goes to bed.
Wakes up. Goes to work.
Does it in first grade everything he does.
And says goodnight with a title track:
It's not easy being me.

[Chorus]
It's not easy being me
Joel Aaron McIvor
It's not easy being me
Forty-five and going
It's not easy being me
But he keeps going anyway
It's not easy being me
That's the song
He named it himself
It's not easy being me

[Bridge - spoken, completely level]
He is the same man who rolled two guards off his back
and asked if that was all they had.
He is the same man who went to see a psychologist
and texted his brother about it.
He is the same man who said
Ari is the best singer in the house
she will be famous.
He is the same man who goes to bed at 8am
and says it's not easy being me.
These are all the same man.
That's what makes the song true.

[Chorus reprise]
It's not easy being me
But I do it anyway
It's not easy being me
Joel — first grade — going
It's not easy being me

[Outro - guitar alone, warm]
Good night bro.
Love you.
Miss ya.
Give the kids a cuddle.
Kiss on the forehead.
From Joel.
It's not easy being me.
But who else would do it.
